result.rationale: The diff shows `useState<string[]>([""])` initializing with an empty row, and MultiEmail lets users add/remove rows freely. `handleAdd` only bails on `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, then runs `z.array(z.string().email()).safeParse` on the raw array. An empty string fails `.email()`, so any leftover blank row makes safeParse fail and the mutation never fires, showing the generic error. This is a real behavioral defect (a user with one filled and one blank row cannot submit), verifiable directly from the diffed code.

judged_text: handleAdd sends the raw multiEmailValue array (which the UI initializes to [""] and keeps as an empty row when a user removes/leaves blanks) instead of validationResult.data, so any remaining empty string fails z.string().email() and blocks the whole submission. A user who adds two emails, fills one, and leaves the second row empty always sees the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error with no indication which row is the problem; the mutation never fires.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `multiEmailValue` is initialized/reset to `[""]` and `handleAdd` validates the entire array with `z.array(z.string().email())` (`safeParse(multiEmailValue)`). If the user leaves any row blank (e.g., adds a second email then leaves it empty), the array contains an empty string and validation fails, so the mutation is never called and the generic `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is shown. The code also checks only `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, so `[""]` still proceeds to validation and fails. While the finding’s mention of not using `validationResult.data` is moot (it would equal the same array), the underlying blocked-submission behavior due to blank entries is verifiable from the diff.
